title: Teaching
text:
Credentials
Foundations for University Teaching in Statistics and Actuarial Science Certificate 



To earn this certificate, graduate students in the University of Waterloo’s Department of Statistics and Actuarial Science are required to attend at least six workshops (two run by the department and at least four run by the university’s Centre for Teaching Excellence) and complete two teaching practicums observed by a member of the department’s TA Program.   My first practicum involved running a 50-minute tutorial on random variable transformations (STAT 330, Fall 2024). My second practicum involved designing and running a two-hour review session on finding maximum likelihood, method of moments, and Bayesian estimators and evaluating their efficiency (STAT 450, Winter 2025). Both were observed by Prof. Reza Ramezan.   More information about the certificate can be found here.

title: A bit about me outside of academia …
text:
Music
I play the piano regularly, with a preference for pieces that sound nice but aren’t too hard to play — many things by Ludovico Einaudi fit this description, and I’ve recently learned “The Breach” and “Dans les bois” from Alexandra Stréliski’s Néo-Romance (see below).

title: A bit about me outside of academia …
text:
Swimming (and other sports)
I swam competitively from the age of eight through the fourth year of my undergraduate degree, a span of about 13 years. I had a lot of fun experiences and learned a great deal about time management and hard work, but these days I am very much a “swammer.” Instead I enjoy participating in intramurals (flag football, volleyball, and soccer so far) and watching tennis.

title: Laura Bumbulis
text:
Welcome! I’m a third-year PhD Candidate in Statistics at the University of Waterloo, working under the supervision of Prof. Richard Cook. I completed my BMath in 2022 and my MMath in Statistics in 2024, both also at the University of Waterloo.
My research interests include multistate modelling under complex observation schemes as well as two-phase designs for failure time studies.
 Department of Statistics and Actuarial Science University of Waterloo

title: Current Professional Activities
text:
I am currently co-chairing (with Benjamin Côté and Jay Sivathayalan) the 6th Waterloo Student Conference in Statistics, Actuarial Science, and Finance !

The conference will take place at the University of Waterloo on October 23–24, 2026.
Submit an abstract here by Monday, September 14.
Register here by Friday, October 9.


More generally, within the Department of Statistics and Actuarial Science at Waterloo:

Since January 2025 I have been co-organizing (first with Megan French, and now with Madison Cranstone) a Student Seminar Series designed to give grad students an opportunity to present their research. We also occasionally invite professors to introduce their work to a student audience.

If you are interested in giving a talk, please reach out!

In June 2025 I began a two-year term as grad student co-representative (with Diribsa Bedada for one year and Victor Malinowski for the other). We facilitate communication between students, faculty, and staff in the department and represent the student perspective at department meetings.
